title: Math and Classical ML
tagline: Enough theory to reason about models, losses, data and failure modes without hand-waving.

topics.title: Linear algebra
topics.summary: The language of embeddings, attention and every tensor op.
items: Vectors, norms, dot product, cosine similarity
Matrices as linear maps, matmul, transpose, inverse
Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, SVD, low-rank approximation (why LoRA works)
PCA and its relation to SVD
Orthogonality, projections, basis, rank
Tensor shapes and broadcasting (NumPy/PyTorch)
questions: Why does cosine similarity work for embeddings and when does it not?
Explain LoRA in terms of low-rank matrices.

topics.title: Calculus and optimization
items: Partial derivatives, gradient, Jacobian, Hessian
Chain rule and backpropagation by hand
Gradient descent, SGD, momentum, RMSProp, Adam, AdamW
Learning rate schedules: warmup, cosine decay
Convexity, saddle points, local minima in high dimensions
Regularization: L1, L2, weight decay, dropout
Vanishing and exploding gradients, gradient clipping
questions: Derive backprop for a two-layer MLP.
Why AdamW over Adam with L2?
Why do transformers need LR warmup?

topics.title: Probability and statistics
topics.summary: Needed for sampling, evals, A/B tests and uncertainty.
items: Random variables, expectation, variance, covariance
Common distributions: Bernoulli, Gaussian, categorical, Poisson
Bayes rule, MLE vs MAP
Entropy, cross-entropy, KL divergence, perplexity
Law of large numbers, CLT, confidence intervals, bootstrap
Hypothesis testing, p-values, power, multiple comparisons
A/B testing design, sample size, sequential testing pitfalls
Sampling: temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p, beam search
Calibration and uncertainty estimation
questions: Why is cross-entropy the right loss for classification?
How many samples do you need to detect a 2% improvement in an eval?

topics.title: Classical machine learning
topics.summary: Often the right answer in production. Always the right baseline.
items: Supervised vs unsupervised vs self-supervised vs RL
Linear and logistic regression
Trees, random forests, gradient boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM)
SVM and kernel idea
k-means, GMM, hierarchical clustering, DBSCAN
Bias-variance trade-off, overfitting, cross-validation
Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, log loss
Imbalanced data: resampling, class weights, threshold tuning
Feature engineering, leakage, train/serve skew
Recommender basics: collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, two-tower
Time series basics and forecasting baselines
scikit-learn pipelines
questions: When would you pick gradient boosting over a neural network?
Explain data leakage with an example.
Precision vs recall: how do you choose a threshold?
